headline: Closed hearings on Brook Street culvert, transmission line, and 30 Argilla Road projects; released over $200,000 in bonds; tabled 38 Atkinson Street demolition.
summary: The Commission closed public hearings on the Brook Street Culvert replacement, the 397 Transmission Line project, and an accessory dwelling unit at 30 Argilla Road. It approved a Negative Determination of Applicability for 28 West Street, released several bonds, and lifted enforcement orders at three properties. A request for work at 38 Atkinson Street was tabled pending Health Department and septic approvals, and most open violation cases were continued to future dates.

CITY OF METHUEN 
CONSERVATION COMMISSION 
Minutes of a Meeting – September 3, 2026 
 
The City of Methuen Conservation Commission held a public hearing and public meeting 
on September 3, 2026, at the Searles Building, 41 Pleasant Street, Second Floor Conference 
Room.  Both the hearing and meeting were hybrid, i.e., permitting both in-person and 
electronic remote participation.  
 
PUBLIC HEARING 
 
1. ROLL CALL 
Present were Dave Di Zazzo, Chair; Kenneth Sateriale, Secretary; Sandra Boulay, 
Commissioner; Rachel Letcher, Commissioner; and Patrice Friant, Commissioner.  A quorum 
was present.  Also present were Chris Parsons, Conservation Officer, and Michelle Davidson, 
Conservation Clerk.  Commissioner Cara Seaman was absent.   
 
2. NOTICES OF INTENT 
No new Notices of Intent were presented. 
 
3. CONTINUED NOTICES OF INTENT 
 
A. Notice of Intent – DEP File #219-1324, MCC File #26-005 – Brook Street Culvert – TEC, 
Inc. – Department of Public Works, Methuen, MA 
(Continued from August 20, 2026) 
Emily Clickner of TEC, Inc. presented the revised proposal for replacement of the existing 
bridge at Brook Street over the Spigot River.  The existing structure is a three-foot-span, dry-laid 
stone culvert with loose and missing stones.  The proposed project includes a nine-and-one-half-
foot span, three-sided precast concrete culvert with cast-in-place wing walls, relocation of 
drainage outlets, sewer and water mains, new riprap aprons, new bridge and approach guardrails, 
roadway resurfacing, streambed restoration, and wetland replication. 
The applicant stated that the project meets five of the six applicable stream-crossing standards.  
The 1.2 bank-full-width standard cannot be met because of site constraints.  (The 1.2 bank-full-
Page 2 
width standard means that a bridge or culvert over a stream must be at least 20% wider than the 
natural width of the stream when it is full 
.)  Water-control measures and sediment-control barriers will be used during construction. 
Maria Johnsenberg of Ty and Bond confirmed that the peer review comments had been 
addressed, with remaining matters limited to recommended conditions.  No public comment was 
received. 
MOTION: Motion made by Kenneth Sateriale to close the hearing.  Seconded by Sandra Boulay.  
All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous.  Hearing closed.  
 
 
B. Notice of Intent – DEP File #219-1321, MCC File #26-002 – 397 Transmission Line Asset 
Condition Refurbishment Project – BSC Group 
(Continued from August 20, 2026) 
The applicant presented responses to the latest peer review comments for the transmission line 
project.  The hydrologic connection remained shown on the environmental resource map, and 
updates were made to WPA Form 3. 
The applicant reported approximately 180 square feet of bordering vegetated wetland impacts 
associated with expanded concrete caisson foundations.  A proposed 180-square-foot wetland 
replication area will be seeded with a native wetland seed mix.  The applicant also proposed 
approximately 1,826 square feet of flood-storage mitigation for approximately 257 cubic feet of 
fill. 
The Commission discussed removal of existing pole bases and associated riprap as in-situ flood-
storage restoration, temporary matting across the Hawks Brook and Bear Meadow Brook areas, 
and the use of an environmental monitor during mat placement and construction. 
Andrew McNulty of Lucas Environmental requested clarification and revisions to the WPA form 
regarding square-footage and cubic-foot calculations, including the distinction between 
construction-mat impacts, foundation impacts, flood-storage loss, and proposed mitigation.  
Lucas Environmental also requested that the resource areas and mean high-water lines be 
properly delineated on the plans. 
The applicant agreed to revise the WPA form and provide clarification before issuance of the 
Order of Conditions. 
MOTION: Motion made by Patrice Friant to close the hearing, subject to receipt of revised 
impact calculations, a revised WPA form, and clarification of the resource-area delineations. 
Seconded by Kenneth Sateriale.  All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous.  Hearing closed.  
 
 
C. Notice of Intent – DEP File #219-1325, MCC File #26-006 – 30 Argilla Road – Nina Piro 
(Continued from August 20, 2026) 
Ben Osgood of Ranger Engineering presented the revised proposal for construction of an 
accessory dwelling unit above an existing garage.  The majority of the work is located beyond 
the 50-foot wetland buffer zone.  The existing driveway will remain undisturbed. 
The applicant proposed installation of a hay-wattle and silt-fence combination along the 
driveway and erosion controls around the soil stockpile.  No additional Commission concerns 
were raised. 
MOTION: Motion made by Sandra Boulay to close the hearing.  Seconded by Kenneth Sateriale.  
All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous.  Hearing closed.  
 
PUBLIC MEETING 
 
4. CALL TO ORDER
Page 3 
The regular public meeting was called to order at 7:38 p.m.  
 
5. ACCEPTANCE OF AGENDA / AMENDMENTS 
The agenda was amended to add the old business item S. 
 
MOTION: Motion made by Kenneth Sateriale to accept the agenda as amended.  Seconded by 
Sandra Boulay.  All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous.  
 
6. ACCEPTANCE OF MINUTES – August 20, 2026 
 
MOTION: Motion made by Kenneth Sateriale to accept the minutes of August 20, 2026.  
Seconded by Patrice Friant.  All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous.  
 
7. NEW BUSINESS 
 
A. Request for Determination of Applicability #26-006 – 28 West Street – Harjinder Singh 
The Commission discussed a proposal to fill and level a recessed area in the rear yard.  The 
proposed work is outside the conservation markers. 
 
MOTION: Motion made by Patrice Friant for a Negative Determination of Applicability under 
Conditions 1- 9.  Seconded by Kenneth Sateriale.  All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous. 
The determination was expected to be available for pickup on Tuesday following the Labor Day 
holiday.  
 
B. Request for Determination of Applicability #26-007 – 38 Atkinson Street – Greg Carlson 
The applicant discussed demolition and environmental cleanup of a fire-damaged property. The 
proposed work includes removal of the structure, pool, associated wooden structures, asbestos-
containing materials, vermiculite, and the septic system after completion of the environmental 
work. 
 
The applicant stated that the work would remain within the established erosion-control area.  The 
Commission noted that Health Department approval, septic-related documentation, and 
installation and inspection of erosion controls had not yet been completed. 
The matter was tabled pending: 
 
• Health Department sign-off; 
• Installation and inspection of erosion controls; and 
• Completion of required septic-related documentation. 
The Commission discussed holding a special meeting before October 1, 2026, subject to quorum 
and scheduling. 
 
MOTION: Motion made by Patrice Friant to table the matter until a special meeting.  Seconded 
by Sandra Boulay.  Vote: Approved unanimously.  
 
8. OLD BUSINESS 
 
A. Notice of Violation #23-004 – Hampshire Road – Joseph Lonigro
Page 4 
The Conservation Officer reported that access to the property was not possible because the gate 
was locked and the driveway was overgrown.  The matter will be revisited in late spring. 
 
MOTION: Motion made by Patrice Friant to continue the matter to May 20, 2027.  Seconded by 
Sandra Boulay.  All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous.  
 
B. Notice of Violation #26-010 – 14 Freeport Street – Wilfred Cyr 
The site was reported to be in compliance following removal of material placed near an 
intermittent stream. Additional time will be allowed for revegetation and monitoring. 
 
MOTION: Motion made by Patrice Friant to continue the matter to May 6, 2027.  Seconded by 
Rachel Letcher.  All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous.  
 
C. Notice of Violation #23-010 – DEP File #219-1195 – Toll Brothers – 26 Phoebe Street 
The site was reported to be in compliance.  The Conservation Officer recommended lifting the 
Notice of Violation. 
 
MOTION: Motion made by Patrice Friant to lift the Notice of Violation.  Seconded by Rachel 
Letcher.  Vote: Approved unanimously.  
 
D. Notice of Violation MCC #23-006 – 109 Milk Street – Alcione Soares 
The site was reported to be in compliance.  The Commission agreed to allow one additional 
growing season. 
 
MOTION: Motion made by Sandra Boulay to continue the matter to May 6, 2027.  Seconded by 
Kenneth Sateriale. All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous.  
 
E. Notice of Violation #23-009 – 60 Pond Street – Whitmer Castro 
The Commission discussed continued maintenance of a grass strip inside the conservation 
markers.  The matter will be monitored for another growing season. 
 
MOTION: Motion made by Patrice Friant to continue the matter to April 15, 2027.  Seconded by 
Rachel Letcher.  All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous.  
 
F. Notice of Violation #25-010 – 14 Myrtle Street – Dennis Holland 
The site was reported to be in compliance.  Additional time was requested to monitor vegetation 
growth. 
 
MOTION: Motion made by Sandra Boulay to continue the matter to April 15, 2027.  Seconded 
by Patrice Friant.  All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous.  
 
G. Notice of Violation #26-009 – 91 Lindbergh Avenue – 91 Lindbergh Avenue, LLC 
The Commission discussed substantial fill placed in or near a floodplain and wetland area 
associated with a perennial stream.  Some material had been removed, and an engineering plan 
was being prepared. 
 
MOTION: Motion made by Patrice Friant to continue the matter to November 6, 2026.  
Seconded by Rachel Letcher.  All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous.
Page 5 
H. Notice of Violation #25-002 / Enforcement Order #25-005 – 39 Tyler Street – Wanderson 
Pimentel 
The site was reported to be in excellent condition.  Additional time will be allowed before review 
for a Certificate of Compliance. 
 
MOTION: Motion made by Patrice Friant to continue the matter to June 3, 2027.  Seconded by 
Sandra Boulay.  Vote: Approved unanimously.  
 
I. Notice of Violation #26-011 – 97 Weybossett Street – Tania Damota 
The Conservation Officer reported that the fence had been repaired and the site had been brought 
substantially into compliance.  Missing conservation markers must be replaced, followed by 
monitoring for two growing seasons. 
 
MOTION: Motion made by Patrice Friant to continue the matter to May 20, 2027.  Seconded by 
Sandra Boulay.  All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous.  
 
J. Notice of Violation #26-012 – 71 Lowell Boulevard – Kathleen Becker and Patricia Howe 
The Commission discussed clearing and improperly installed erosion controls in a floodplain 
area associated with a proposed approximately 4,900-square-foot addition.  The property was 
placed under a cease-and-desist order. 
An engineered plan showing the floodplain must be submitted. 
 
MOTION: Motion made by Patrice Friant to continue the matter to November 5, 2026.  
Seconded by Rachel Letcher.  All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous.  
 
K. Enforcement Order #24-006 – 91 Sevoian Drive – Gramstorff 
The property was reported to be substantially in compliance.  Additional growing time and 
reinspection were requested. 
 
MOTION: Motion made by Sandra Boulay to continue the matter to June 3, 2027.  Seconded by 
Kenneth Sateriale.  All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous.  
 
L. Enforcement Order #24-004 – 47 Tedesco Road – Malik Ruzayqat 
The property was reported to be in compliance following restoration work near an intermittent 
stream. 
 
MOTION: Motion made by Sandra Boulay to continue the matter to June 3, 2027.  Seconded by 
Kenneth Sateriale.  All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous.  
 
M. Enforcement Order #24-005 – 48 Kensington Avenue – Frank Sergi 
The property owner was reported to have remained compliant and completed the required 
restoration and revegetation. 
 
MOTION: Motion made by Sandra Boulay to lift the Enforcement Order.  Seconded by Kenneth 
Sateriale.  All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous.  Enforcement Order #24-005 was lifted.  
 
N. Notice of Violation #23-011 / Enforcement Order #23-006 – 510 Lowell Street, LLC 
The property was reported to be in compliance, including removal of pavement and erosion 
controls from the restoration area.
Page 6 
MOTION: Motion made by Patrice Friant to lift the Enforcement Order.  Seconded by Kenneth 
Sateriale.  All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous.  Enforcement Order #23-006 was lifted.  
 
O. Request for Certificate of Compliance and Bond Release – $34,500.00 – DEP File #219-
1289, MCC File #23-003 – 65 Haverhill Street – Amigos Coffee, LLC 
The site was reported to be compliant. 
 
MOTION: Motion made by Sandra Boulay to issue the Certificate of Compliance and release the 
$34,500.00 bond.  Seconded by Kenneth Sateriale.  All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous.  
 
P. Bond Release – $146,100.00 – DEP File #219-1250, MCC File #20-009 – 33 Danton Drive 
– 47R Danton Landowner, LLC 
 
MOTION: Motion made by Rachel Letcher to release the $146,100.00 bond.  Seconded by 
Patrice Freon.  All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous.  
 
Q. Bond Release – $17,600.00 – DEP File #219-1315, MCC File #25-003 – 175 Pelham Street 
– Grieco Automotive Group 
The agenda listed a bond amount of $17,600.00.  The motion and discussion referred to release 
of $17,600.00.  The amount should be verified against the official paperwork. 
 
MOTION: Motion made by Rachel Letcher to release the bond.  Seconded by Patrice Friant. All 
in favor.  Vote: Unanimous. 
 
R. Bond Release – $4,800.00 – DEP File #219-1313, MCC File #28-001 – 65 Ormonde Road – 
Cristina Stonionis. 
 
MOTION: Motion made by Rachel Letcher to release the $4,800.00 bond.  Seconded by Patrice 
Friant.  All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous.  
 
9. CONSERVATION OFFICER’S REPORT 
The Commission discussed unresolved Health Department, septic, and permitting issues related 
to 38 Atkinson Street.  The required documentation and erosion-control inspection must be 
completed before the RDA can be issued. 
The Commission discussed coordinating a special meeting before October 1, 2026, to address the 
38 Atkinson Street RDA and issue Orders of Conditions for the previously closed public 
hearings, subject to receipt of the required materials. 
  
10. OTHER BUSINESS 
 
A. Vote to Adopt the Methuen Conservation Commission Roles and Responsibilities Guide 
The Commission discussed the Field Conservation Rules and Responsibilities Guide. 
 
MOTION: Motion made by Rachel Letcher to adopt the Methuen Conservation Rules and 
Responsibilities Guide.  Seconded by Patrice Friant.  All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous.  
 
B. Review of Public Hearing vs. Public Meeting and Vote to Adopt Three-Minute Rule 
 
The Commission reviewed the distinction between public hearings and regular public meetings.
Page 7 
The Commission discussed a proposed three-minute public-comment rule, including the need for 
orderly and efficient meetings and the Chair’s discretion to allow additional time when necessary 
to complete a presentation.  The Commission agreed that the draft language should be revised to 
clarify the Chair’s discretion. 
The vote on the three-minute rule was deferred until a future regular meeting.  The matter will 
not be considered at the special meeting.  
 
11. ADJOURNMENT 
There being no further business, a motion to adjourn was made by Kenneth Sateriale and 
seconded by Patrice Friant.  All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous.  The meeting adjourned at 
approximately 8:38 p.m. 
  
Respectfully submitted by, 
 
Dave Di Zazzo
